note: Connects governance structures to specific deployment risks in healthcare, useful when scoping an audit for a provider organisation.
title: Scaling enterprise AI in healthcare: the role of governance in risk mitigation frameworks
explain_beginner: This viewpoint paper asks how rules and oversight can help healthcare groups use artificial intelligence more safely. The authors say that because AI changes quickly, strong oversight is needed to handle possible harmful events and to support innovation that treats people fairly, promotes equity, and works well. They point out major dangers tied to putting AI into use and suggest ways to improve oversight across an organization. The paper matters because healthcare choices affect people directly. Without good oversight, AI could create trust problems or uneven care. The authors argue that better oversight can help groups manage those dangers while still encouraging useful progress in digital health.
explain_business: For executives, this paper says healthcare AI adoption needs strong oversight, not just technical tools. The authors argue that good governance helps reduce risk, manage possible harmful events, and build confidence. It also supports innovation that treats people fairly, promotes equity, and works well. The paper identifies dangers tied to putting AI into use and suggests improvements to oversight across the organization. The editor note says the work connects oversight structures to specific risks, which can help leaders define an audit for a provider group. In practice, this informs decisions about whether to strengthen governance and how to scope an audit.
explain_practitioner: The authors present a viewpoint paper rather than an experiment. They examine how oversight structures can lower risk and raise confidence when healthcare groups put artificial intelligence into service. The work identifies important dangers tied to these uses and recommends changes to oversight at the organization level. Its main result is a call to strengthen governance so it can better meet the challenges created by AI and digital health tools. The editor note adds that the paper links oversight structures to particular risks from use, which can help when defining the scope of an audit for a care provider.
